column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“All the days” is rendered “perpetually.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Spoke” is rendered “promised,” and “will not be cut off to you” as “You shall not lack.”
“Descendants” is rendered “sons,” and “bow down” as “worship.”
“A byword and a taunt” is rendered “a proverb and a byword.”
The Hebrew reads “this house will be most high”; NASB renders “will become a heap of ruins,” following some ancient versions.
“Took hold on” is rendered “adopted,” and “calamity” as “adversity.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB carries the sentence through verse 11.
“Supported” is rendered “supplied”; NASB puts the first part in parentheses.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Someone called them” is rendered “they were called.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“The word of” is rendered “the account of,” and “raised” as “levied.”
“Dowries” is rendered “a dowry.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The written Hebrew reads “Tamar” and the reading tradition “Tadmor”; NASB has “Tamar” and supplies “of Judah.”
“The desire of Solomon” is rendered “all that it pleased Solomon,” and “land of his dominion” as “land under his rule.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Forced labor of laboring” is rendered “forced laborers.”
“Officials” is rendered “princes,” and “officers” as “captains.”
“Leaders of the overseers” is rendered “chief officers.”
“Only” is rendered “As soon as.”
“Made smoke with it” is rendered “burning incense with them.” The Hebrew is difficult.
“Sea of reeds” is rendered “Red Sea,” and “ships” as “a fleet of ships.”
“Men of ships” is rendered “sailors.”
Close to the Hebrew.
